newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end slightly lower, yen strengthens.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end slightly lower, yen strengthens.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed barely lower on Thursday after the yen's rebound against the dollar helped recover the majority of early losses, brokers said.
Kia Motors and Asia Motors surged to their daily upper limits on the possibility of a third-party takeover, they said.

"The yen's rise helped improve sentiment. But the market was basically dull, reflected in the low trading volume. The tone is likely to continue for the time being," said Jeon Jeong-tak, a broker at Hyundai Secuities.
The composite stock index ended off 0.77 to 726.12 points.
Volume totalled 25.83 million shares compared with 25.48 million on Wednesday. Gainers outpaced losers 422 to 322 with 153 stocks unchanged.
Brokers said the central bank's supply of 800 billion won through repurchase agreements caused interest rates to fall briefly, imrpoving investor sentiment.
But interest rates went up again due to tightening liquidity as a result of tax and salary payments at the end of July.
POSCO began recovering from several days of losses in the afternoon on the belief that the stock was oversold.
POSCO had been hit by its plan to buy part of the troubled Hanbo Steel's assets, which was viewed as a move that would erode the company's profitability.
Moody's Investors Service said on Thursday it had placed the A2 senior unsecured debt ratings of POSCO under review for possible downgrade in light of the company's offer on Hanbo.
"POSCO shares will likely fall because of the Moody's report. But the purchase plan has been almost fully reflected," said Na Min-ho of Daishin Securities.
The yen strengthened to 117.70 per dollar from 118.40 level on Wednesday.
Brokers said fears of falling chip prices hit shares of Samsung Electronics, which dropped 600 won to 64,900.
KEPCO dropped 900 won to 26,000 after facing sales by foreign investors.
Brokers said expectations of an early expansion of the foreign stock ownership limit could boost sentiment on Friday.
If the government plans to raise the ceiling in September, the announcement should be made this week, they said.
The limit was raised to 23 percent in May from 20 percent and it was to be raised further to 25 to 26 percent before the end of this year, the finance ministry has said.
